chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: Hakam ibn Hukaym al-Sayrafi narrated to me, he said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What do you say regarding a dog that hunts prey and kills it? He said: There is no problem with eating it.

He said: I said: But they say that if it kills it and eats from it, then it has only kept it for itself, so do not eat it. He said: Eat! Have they not already agreed with you that if it kills it, that is its ritual slaughter? I said: Yes.

He said: So what do they say regarding a sheep that a man slaughtered — has he purified it? I said: Yes. He said: But if a wild beast came after he had slaughtered it and ate part of it, would the remainder be eaten? I said: Yes.

He said: So when they answer you to this, say to them: How do you say that when that one (the dog) slaughtered and ate from it you do not eat, yet when this one (the man) slaughtered it and it (the wild beast) ate, you do eat?

key_terms.السَّبُع: Wild beast/predator — used as a counter-analogy to expose the inconsistency of the opposing ruling
key_terms.الصَّيْد: Hunt/game — the prey caught by a trained hunting animal
key_terms.ذَكَاة: Ritual slaughter (tazkiya) — the act that renders an animal's flesh lawful for consumption; in this context applied to a hunting dog's kill
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem/harm — a standard jurisprudential formula indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat game killed by a hunting dog if the dog ate some of it?
ai.summary: This hadith records a jurisprudential dialogue between Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and Hakam ibn Hukaym al-Sayrafi on the permissibility of consuming game killed by a hunting dog, even if the dog ate part of it. The Imam employs a logical analogy (qiyas al-awla): since a man's ritual slaughter of a sheep remains valid even if a wild beast later eats from it, so too the dog's kill — which the jurists themselves agree constitutes its ritual slaughter — remains lawful for consumption even if the dog ate part. The historical audience included students debating Sunni jurists' positions, and the Imam demonstrates the internal inconsistency of the opposing view.
